h1: What makes a great brewery name
title: How to choose a brewery name | Craft Beer School
desc: Six tests for a strong brewery name, a scorecard for your shortlist and how to check pronunciation across Indian cities.
teaser: The name goes on every can, sign and invoice for years. Test it before you print it.
standfirst: A brewery name has to be free to use, easy to say in Pune and Hyderabad and big enough to carry every beer you will brew. Here are the tests we run on a shortlist.
sections: Your name does its work before anyone sees the logo

Long before a guest tastes your beer, they hear the name from a friend, see it on a food app or type it into Instagram. The name introduces you before any artwork does. A weak one can follow you for years.

We test every shortlist against six qualities: available, different, easy to spell and remember, enjoyable to say, flexible and portable. Each gets a section below, adapted for a brewpub or microbrewery opening in India. This guide is about the brewery name. Naming individual beers is a separate job, covered in naming a beer brand.
Availability comes first, before anyone falls in love

Run this test before any other. Search for breweries, wineries, distilleries and drinks brands with the same or a similar name, in India and abroad. Check the .in and .com domains and the Instagram handle.

Then search the public trademark records of the Trade Marks Registry at ipindia.gov.in. Beer sits in Nice class 32, other alcoholic drinks in class 33 and taproom or restaurant services in class 43, so a close match in any of those three classes is a warning sign. Our guide to trademarking a brewery name in India explains the process. Have a trademark attorney check the name before you print a single coaster. Repainting a sign and reprinting menus after launch costs more than a search done first.
Different means it points at something only you have

The second test is that the name reflects what sets you apart: a brewing method, the founders' story or the place. In India that might be the neighbourhood, an old building, a local ingredient or a family trade. A name that could hang over any of the dozens of brewpubs in Bengaluru tells nobody anything.

Be wary of the invented word. Made-up names are often easy to register, but they mean nothing on day one, so your branding has to do all the explaining. If you choose one, make sure you can tell its story in 2 sentences on the back of the menu.
Say it out loud in five cities

Easy to spell, easy to remember and fun to say covers three of the six. In India add a harder test: will it survive five languages and a bad phone line?

Read each shortlisted name to 10 people from Bengaluru, Pune, Gurugram, Mumbai and Hyderabad. Then ask them to:

  • spell it back after hearing it once, as if typing it into Instagram search;
  • repeat it into a WhatsApp voice note so someone else can write down what they heard;
  • check it in Kannada, Marathi, Hindi and Telugu for an unlucky meaning or slang;
  • write it in Devanagari or Kannada script and see whether the sound holds.

If 3 of the 10 cannot spell it, people will struggle to find you online. A name that means something rude in one city will be the only thing that city remembers about you.
A good name survives a second outlet

Flexibility and portability close the list. Flexibility means the name can carry a theme across 6 to 10 beers, events and merchandise. Portability means it still works when you open a second outlet in another city or send cans across state lines, where label approval and excise rules differ again.

Avoid a joke that only one neighbourhood gets, or a trend that will feel dated in three years. Then check the name at the sizes it will appear most: on a 330 ml can, on a tap handle and as a phone-sized Instagram profile picture. Long names that look grand on a signboard often turn to mush at that last size.
Score the shortlist and pick a winner

Bring 3 to 5 names to the table and score each from 1 to 5 on the six tests, for a maximum of 30. Any name that scores 1 on availability is out, whatever its total. Then ask the question no scorecard answers: would the team be proud to say it every day for 10 years?

An outside eye with advertising experience helps here, because founders tend to fall for the first name they thought of. For this week, write 20 candidate names, cut them to 5 and run the availability checks on each before you share any of them outside the founding team.
Ankur Napa is a Master Brewer who also works in data and AI. Chatty Girija spent more than 30 years in advertising, hosts the Cheers Chatty Beer Podcast and teaches at Craft Beer School.
faqs: Should a brewery name include the word brewing or brewery?
It helps people know what you are, especially on maps and in search. It does not make a taken name available, so run the trademark checks either way.
Can we use our city or neighbourhood in the name?
Yes, it tells a clear story. Place names alone are hard to protect and can limit a second outlet, so pair the place with something only you own.
Do we need a registered trademark before we open?
We are not lawyers and cannot advise on that. Search the Trade Marks Registry records early and have a trademark attorney check your shortlist before anything is printed.
